speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the severity and location of your issue, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ptosis-induced diplopia that worsens with upward/downward gaze, along with fatigable limb weakness that improves with rest and lacks sensory or cerebellar signs, is classic for this autoimmune disorder.
